#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The data for prerelease was obtained from adding a test to `roundtrip_test.go` to get all the prerelease information, a very fuzzy gvk -> gvr replace, and matching the prerelease information to the corresponding gvr in `test/integration/etcd/data.go`. Here is the [raw data](https://gist.github.com/Jefftree/24c9ad2f9757d62fb91d18bf839f62ee)

```
func TestGenFixtureData(t *testing.T) {
	scheme := runtime.NewScheme()
	for _, builder := range groups {
		if err := builder.AddToScheme(scheme); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected error adding to scheme: %v", err)
		}
	}
	for gvk, _ := range scheme.AllKnownTypes() {
		o, err := scheme.New(gvk)
		if err != nil {
			panic(err)
		}
		oWithIntroduced, ok := o.(introducedInterface)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		major, minor := oWithIntroduced.APILifecycleIntroduced()
		t.Logf("%s.%s.%s, Introduced: %d.%d\n", gvk.Group, gvk.Version, strings.ToLower(gvk.Kind)+"s", major, minor)

		oWithRemoved, ok := o.(removedInterface)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		major, minor = oWithRemoved.APILifecycleRemoved()
		t.Logf("%s.%s.%s, Removed: %d.%d\n", gvk.Group, gvk.Version, strings.ToLower(gvk.Kind)+"s", major, minor)

	}
}

type introducedInterface interface {
	APILifecycleIntroduced() (major, minor int)
}
type removedInterface interface {
	APILifecycleRemoved() (major, minor int)
}
```

issue_context.title: etcd compatibility fixtures should derive version rather than hard code when APIs were introduced/removed
comments:
@liggitt: Have a quick question about the derivation. We hard code the fixtures in etcd so that accidental changes to the types will cause the tests to fail and require an etcd fixture update. An update is required in two places for any lifecycle changes, the lifecycle file as well as the etcd fixtures. 

For instance, if I decided to mark an api's lifecycle as removed, I need to remove the corresponding fixture in `data.go`. If we dynamically derive these, the existence of the types in `data.go` will be directly affected by a file's prerelease tags. If a type is removed via changing the api's prerelease tags, no changes are needed to the corresponding fixture in `data.go`. We're reducing the "update two places" to "only update one location".

Wouldn't this go against the purpose of having the fixture in the first place? Would it make more sense to hard code the introduced and removed versions here so that two locations need to be changed for an API lifecycle change?

For example 

```
		gvr("resource.k8s.io", "v1beta1", "deviceclasses"): {
			Stub:             `{"metadata": {"name": "class2name"}}`,
			ExpectedEtcdPath: "/registry/deviceclasses/class2name",
			Introduced: "1.31",
			Removed: "1.37", 
		},
```
hmm... I guess that makes sense... hopefully it won't be a huge pain to set the same data in two places like that

review_comments: Issue discovered in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128279#discussion_r1908013803. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129416 will fix it and remove the need for this line

to minimize the diff, would it make sense to only add this for APIs added / removed >=1.31 where emulated version is relevant, and assume APIs without these explicitly set are available in all versions?

I included the information so that future API additions have a proper reference and we can properly lint for the fields being present. This technically extends to almost APIs added since 1.25 since our 6 cycle removal policy would point to 1.31 or later removal. I don't think the diff is that much larger when reviewing with "hide whitespace changes" and the versions were programmatically generated. Open to removing if you still feel like it's a big change though.

it'll change the blame on ~all the lines in the data file, which is a touch annoying, and I didn't really want to review / verify all the version lines that don't really matter, but I guess it's not a huge deal

This resource does not have proper lifecycle information. Adding lifecycle information would imply a removedVersion being set but this alpha API has been around for years already and I'm not sure if it's something that can be easily set.
